status_detail: Creston News Advertiser described Southwest Iowa REC as owner of the sole data center in Union County while reporting the county's 2026 data center moratorium and committee work.
notes: County minutes on 2026-03-18 formed a data center committee and moved forward with up to a one-year moratorium on development and operation of Data Centers & High-Density Computing Facilities; article says Southwest Iowa REC had representation as owner of the sole county data center.

status_detail: Local TV/Facebook snippets reported a Texas-based company had approached officials with a data center proposal; county subsequently moved toward a moratorium. No formal project name, site, or developer was verified in official minutes found during this pass.

status_detail: County officials were working on data center rules, but local reporting stated no developer had formally approached the county yet.
notes: KYOU reported Supervisor Bryan Ziegler said Wapello County lacked a data center ordinance and was working toward one; the same story said no developer had formally approached Wapello or Jefferson counties yet. A 2026-06-02 county minutes PDF mentions public discussion of data centers and moratorium/ordinance concerns but no named project.

status_detail: Microsoft data center campus in West Des Moines spanning Warren and Madison counties; official announcement described 200 acres, including 160 acres in Warren County and 40 acres in Madison County. Tracker listings show multiple 57 MW operating buildings in Warren County.
notes: Capacity is inferred from tracker-reported 6 Warren County Microsoft/Azure facilities at 57 MW each; official city/economic-development release gives investment, footprint, phases, and county split but not MW. Year set to first operating buildings in tracker; campus has later buildings through at least 2025.

aliases: Norwalk SW Development Corridor data center
status_detail: Norwalk City Council approved a development agreement with Tract/IALCO Warren County Two LLC on March 5, 2026 for a 282-acre site that could be used for a future data center; city said future data center approval would require separate review.
notes: DCD reports Project West is described on the city's development website as a future data center project, with anticipated total investment around $12B, 282 acres west of Highway 28 and south of Delaware Street, approximately 600 construction jobs and 80 full-time high-quality jobs. City notice emphasizes the March 2026 vote did not itself approve construction of a data center.

status_detail: County is studying data-center zoning; no publicly received large-scale proposal found.
notes: County planning agenda references a Subcommittee on Data Centers and June 1, 2026 minutes record a motion to research and develop additional zoning restrictions/requirements for data center development. Decorah News reported no publicly received large-scale proposal, though smaller projects were said to be emerging without enough detail to create a project row.

status_detail: MidAmerican Energy/Midwest Capital Group has options on about 900 acres annexed by Salix and is evaluating the site for a potential data center; local reporting says Google expressed interest in exploring a future data center there. Woodbury County adopted a 12-month moratorium for unincorporated areas, but the Salix site is within the incorporated/annexed city area and is not covered by the county moratorium.
notes: IPR says Salix voluntarily annexed about 900 acres in April 2026; MidAmerican confirmed the location is being considered and its affiliate acquired options to transfer to a future electric customer. KTIV later reported Google interest, while stating MidAmerican characterized it as exploration rather than an approved project.

project_name: Woodbury County unincorporated data center moratorium
status_detail: Woodbury County Board of Supervisors passed a 12-month moratorium on accepting, processing, considering, or approving data center development applications in unincorporated areas on June 23, 2026.
notes: This is not a named facility but is included to capture an official county action directly affecting all unincorporated data center projects. Resolution 14064 also says the moratorium does not affect legally existing facilities or applications with final approvals before the effective date; county/news sources stated they knew of no already approved unincorporated projects.
